newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end weaker, pork bellies mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end weaker, pork bellies mostly higher.

text.p: CME hog futures generally held losses at the close and pork bellies were mostly higher as word a major packer was reducing slaughter operations influnced pork complex futures trade, floor sources said.

Hog futures ended 0.650 cent per lb lower to 0.050 higher with August off most at 81.375 cents. Pork bellies closed up 0.925 cent a lb to off 0.775 cent with August up most at 84.575 cents. July expired earlier at 85.100, up 0.500 cent.
IBP Inc said it would cut back production at hog slaughter plants which weighed on hog futures while prompting short covering in pork bellies, traders said.
IBP said it will cut operating hours at all of its pork plants by at least another four hours and eliminate the Saturday kill at three plants due to tight hog supplies.

Also, expectations hog runs will increase as cooler weather moves into the Midwest and technical resistance weighed on hog futures. But the discount futures hold to the CME lean hog index limited the setback, traders said.
The latest CME lean hog index was quoted at $83.43 per cwt.
